Theme

Latin word

caput

caput, capitis n.

noun, third declension

a capital city; civil status, citizenship; head; section, paragraph, chapter (of a writing); the main point; a section or head of a law or a writing; a chapter; the source of a river; the fountainhead

In this lexicon

  • capital

    the recommended word · classical · Liv. 1.16.7; Liv. 9.37.12: capita Etrūriae populōrum; Traupman 198, 203; M-O s.v. capital (seat of government); Traupman 286

  • civil rights

    also used · classical · Cic. Top. 18: sē capite dēminuere (Lewis & Short s.v. dēminuō)

  • head

    the recommended word · classical · Traupman 58

  • paragraph

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Agr. 2.15: ā prīmō capite lēgis ūsque ad extrēmum (Lewis & Short); Gell. 2.15.4 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 30, 356

  • point

    also used · classical · Cic. Att. 1.17.4: id quod caput est; Traupman 105: that’s the main point, id caput est; Traupman 106: the point is that I no longer care about such things, quod caput est, jam ista nōn cūrō

  • section

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Att. 3.15.6: quoddam caput lēgis; Plin. Ep. 10.114.3; Traupman 273 (a clause in a law or a treaty); Levi–Bini p. 7; Traupman 26, 28: caput quārtum, chapter four; M-O s.v. parts: chapter (division of book); Traupman 29: heading; Traupman 289

  • source

    also used · classical · Hor. S. 1.10.37 (M-O s.v. source (of river)); Traupman 383
